text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $131.77, extending a two-week slide of nearly 3%. The immediate trigger was yesterday's news that Saudi Arabia is releasing more crude oil into the market through the Strait of Hormuz after a pipeline attack disrupted some exports—additional supply typically pressures oil prices downward, and crude has indeed stayed flat to weak despite ongoing Middle East tensions. The stock's slide accelerated on September 16th when it dropped $8.70 in a single day, coinciding with that Saudi supply announcement.

The broader context is that while geopolitical risks in the Middle East remain real—the UN report on civilian casualties and ongoing Saudi-Houthi clashes create real disruption fears—markets are increasingly focused on supply solutions rather than supply shocks. If major producers can offset losses and keep crude flowing, the upside from geopolitical fear tends to fade, which is working against energy stocks like this one in the near term.
